transcript: Slow New Year's Day, exactly the way I wanted it. Slept in properly for the first time in weeks, didn't set an alarm, just let my body decide when it was done. Spent most of the day in pajamas, ate leftover snacks from last night, watched something forgettable on the couch. No big resolutions or grand plans, just wanted one day of genuinely doing nothing before the year picks up speed.
Mundane Friday, first real day back to a normal schedule. Nothing exciting, just easing back into routine. Ordered dinner instead of cooking, still in holiday-mode laziness a little.

Cold run this morning, genuinely cold, the kind where your face goes numb before your legs even warm up. Pushed through it anyway. First run of the new year feels like it should mean something even though logically it's just another Saturday. Legs a little rusty from the holiday break but it felt good to be back out there.

Grocery run and meal prep for the week, trying to actually start the year with some structure instead of just winging every dinner. Chopped a bunch of vegetables, made a big pot of something I'll probably be eating for days. Small satisfaction in having the fridge actually stocked with real food for once.

First proper Monday back, overcast of course, felt like a slap after the holiday quiet. Real back-to-work slump today, hard to get going, hard to care about the things that felt urgent before the break. Atlas is apparently still grinding along in the background, waiting for me. Coffee helping only marginally.

Atlas is still grinding, apparently the holiday break didn't actually pause it the way I'd hoped. Back into the late-afternoon status meetings, the same conversations circling the same blockers. Tired of hearing about it honestly, but not much choice except to keep pushing my piece forward.

Mundane commute, nothing to report really. Work droning on. Signed up for that pottery class Maya kept mentioning, starts Thursday, feeling a little nervous about it honestly since I have zero experience, but figured why not try something completely unrelated to a screen for once.

First pottery class tonight, and I was genuinely terrible at it, like laughably bad. The wheel has a mind of its own and mine kept collapsing into this sad little wobbling lump no matter what I did with my hands. The instructor was patient about it, said everyone's first attempt looks like a disaster and mine apparently wasn't even the worst in the room, small comfort. But something about it got its hooks into me anyway, the clay under your hands, the total focus it demands where you can't think about Atlas or anything else because if your mind wanders the whole thing just falls apart. Came home with clay under my fingernails and a weird kind of calm I haven't felt in weeks. Already looking forward to next Thursday, which surprises me.

Date night with Sam, third one now I think, and it keeps getting easier, less first-date performance and more just being ourselves around each other. We tried that new taco place that's been getting attention, food was good, conversation better. There's a comfort settling in that I wasn't expecting this fast, in a good way.
Saturday errands, nothing thrilling, bank stuff, picked up a prescription, wandered a hardware store for a shelf bracket I still haven't actually installed. Quiet, functional day.

Longer run today, testing my legs out for something bigger, I've been eyeing a ten k in a couple weeks and wanted to see if the distance felt doable. It did, more or less, tired by the end but not destroyed. Putting it on the calendar officially now. Feels good to have a concrete goal instead of just running for the sake of it.

Overcast again, that same flat gray Monday light, and I said something out loud to myself in the car this morning that I haven't actually said before, at least not in those exact words. I'm burnt out. Not tired, not stressed, actually burnt out. Atlas has been going since early December without any real break, the bad sleep stretch back then never fully resolved, it just went quieter, and now it's back, waking up at four most nights with my mind already running through blockers before I've even opened my eyes. Priya's been decent about it, checking in more than my old manager ever did, but the work itself hasn't slowed down and I don't see it slowing down soon. Saying the actual words felt like some kind of threshold, like naming it makes it real in a way that just feeling exhausted didn't. Not sure what I do with that yet. Going to sit with it for now.

Flat workday, going through the motions more than actually engaging with anything. Yesterday's realization still sitting heavy. Didn't have much energy for anything after work, just sat on the couch scrolling my phone longer than I meant to.

Dinner with Tom, good timing honestly, needed the distraction. He's finally made a decision about the job thing he's been agonizing over since November, taking the offer. Happy for him, genuinely, and talking through someone else's big decision for a change was a nice break from stewing in my own stuff.

Pottery class two tonight, still pretty lopsided results if I'm being honest, my bowl looks more like a shallow dish that's had a rough week, but I noticed I was way less anxious about it than my expectations from last time. Progress isn't always visible in the clay itself I guess.

Body just tired today, that heavy end-of-week feeling settling in early this time. Went to bed early, didn't push through anything, figured rest was more useful than forcing myself to be productive on fumes.

Training run in the rain, ten k prep continuing. Got properly soaked, but I've decided that's basically par for the course this winter, rain or overcast, rarely anything in between. Legs felt strong today though, further than expected without needing to walk, so that's encouraging heading into the actual race.

Overcast Monday, restless all through the morning, hard to sit still at my desk for more than twenty minutes at a stretch. Coffee not really cutting through it. Counting down to Thursday pottery already, which has become the thing I actually look forward to most weeks now.

Small design win today, one I actually feel good about, a flow I'd been stuck on for two weeks finally clicked into something clean. Priya noticed it too, said something genuinely complimentary in front of the team, which after last month's rough review felt like it mattered more than usual. Taking the win.

Movie night with Sam, low key, just my couch and a film neither of us had strong opinions about beforehand. Nice to have someone to just exist quietly with after a long stretch of grinding through Atlas. These easy evenings are starting to feel like the thing I most look forward to during the week.

Pottery class three, and I actually made something that resembles a cup this time, lopsided, a little thick on one side, but recognizably a cup, which feels like real progress from the collapsing lumps of week one. The instructor said the rim needs work but the form is there. Small victories.

Quiet Friday night, laying out gear for tomorrow's ten k already, checking the weather forecast obsessively even though there's nothing I can do about it either way. Nervous energy building. Going to bed early to try to actually be rested for once.

Pre-race nerves in full effect tonight, laid everything out for tomorrow morning three separate times just to be sure. Never actually raced a distance like this before, always just running for myself, so there's a different kind of nervousness attached to it having a bib number and a start time. Trying to just trust the training at this point, there's nothing more to do tonight except sleep, if I can manage it.

I did it, first ten k done, official time around sixty four minutes, which honestly exceeded whatever quiet expectation I'd let myself have. Cold this morning, properly cold, breath coming out in these thick clouds at the start line while everyone shuffled around trying to stay warm. Around mile four I genuinely didn't think I had it in me to keep the pace, legs screaming, but something just clicked into a rhythm and I pushed through it. Crossing the finish line, hearing my name called even though nobody I knew was there to see it, some stranger just reading off the chip time, still felt like a real moment. Proud of myself in a way I don't let myself feel that often. Two and a half months ago I could barely run a mile and a half without stopping. Going to let myself sit in this feeling for the rest of the day before going back to worrying about Atlas.

Sore legs today, unsurprisingly, walking down stairs is a whole event. Rain outside instead of the usual overcast for variety. Work was fine, still riding a little bit of yesterday's good feeling into the week, which helped get through some otherwise tedious meetings.
Mundane Tuesday, Atlas grinding along as usual, nothing new to report. Legs still a little sore from the weekend but improving. Early night planned, trying to bank some actual rest for once.

Ordinary commute, gray skies threatening rain that never quite arrived. Work steady, nothing dramatic either direction. Starting to think about calling Mom again this weekend to check on Nonna, been meaning to for a couple weeks and keep letting the week swallow it up.

Pottery again tonight, chatting with a couple of the other regulars in the class while our pieces spun on the wheels, one of them's apparently been doing this for years and gave me some genuinely useful tips about hand pressure. Nice little community forming there without me really trying for it. My cup from last week held up in the kiln at least, first fired piece, feels like a small milestone.

Sam came over for dinner tonight, cooked together instead of just ordering something, a pasta thing that turned out better than expected given neither of us really knew what we were doing halfway through. Easy comfortable evening, the kind that makes a month of Atlas exhaustion feel a little more bearable in retrospect.

Month-end errands, nothing exciting. Looking back at January it's been a lot, the burnout admission, the pottery thing sticking way more than I expected, the ten k, Sam. Hoping February brings a little more breathing room on the Atlas front, though I'm not holding my breath on that one.
